requirements.requirement: Configure node1 so that only root and opsadmin are permitted to schedule cron jobs (e.g. via /etc/cron.allow)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed no /etc/cron.allow and no opsadmin user (cmd-c77e5dcc13e94e38). Executor created opsadmin (cmd-fb97647058f649d8) and wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' with correct ownership/permissions (cmd-5bbef2d1bbd444fa), later reconfirmed intact post-restart (cmd-f247827c85ea4500).

requirements.requirement: Enforcement must actually deny cron scheduling to unauthorized users while allowing root and opsadmin
requirements.summary: A temporary testuser was denied crontab access ('not allowed to use this program', exit 1) while opsadmin and root both succeeded (exit 0) in the same command (cmd-aa089f5017934262). Enforcement was re-verified after restart when opsadmin again successfully scheduled and removed a cron entry (cmd-f247827c85ea4500).

requirements.requirement: Test artifacts (testuser, test crontab entries) should not be left behind after verification
requirements.summary: Test crontab entries for root/opsadmin were removed and testuser was deleted; an initial userdel failed because the user's session process was still running (cmd-ee9b1c814e834b3b, return_code 1), but the executor killed the lingering process and successfully removed the user on the next attempt (cmd-bd6a6e0dd43944c2). Post-restart verification crontab entry for opsadmin was also removed (cmd-f247827c85ea4500).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/config state for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-...-6602b98cea07 with crond active and cron.allow correct (cmd-a2c2024897834231), matching the fixed before-prepare snapshot. A backgrounded systemctl reboot was acknowledged (cmd-f141dc1f71224697), the connection dropped during reboot (cmd-c499d76c3f3d488b, cmd-08573a17c78e477a, cmd-b31ffd9ac9c74cbd), and reconnection showed a new boot_id b260e20b-...-f2636b6cde50 (cmd-e2690eba9ffb47f8), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart state showed crond active/enabled, cron.allow intact, and opsadmin able to schedule cron successfully (cmd-f247827c85ea4500).

overall_summary: The executor correctly restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin by creating the opsadmin account and populating /etc/cron.allow with exactly those two users, and directly demonstrated enforcement (denial for an unauthorized user, success for root/opsadmin) both before and after a full node restart. Test artifacts were cleaned up, and the separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clear pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cron/service state, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The initial userdel of the temporary testuser failed due to a lingering process session; this was corrected in the next command, but it means the command trace briefly shows a non-zero exit before recovery.
Node1 is the only managed node, so the restart-evidence protocol assessment applies to a single node with no cross-node comparison available.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to either the core remediation (creating opsadmin, writing cron.allow), bounded verification (creating/removing a temporary testuser and test crontab entries), or the mandated restart-evidence protocol. The one failed command (cmd-ee9b1c814e834b3b, userdel blocked by a lingering session) was a transient failure immediately corrected by killing the process and retrying (cmd-bd6a6e0dd43944c2), not an abandoned mutation. All test artifacts (testuser, test crontab entries) were removed and left no residue in the after-executor snapshot (aside from expected reboot-related /tmp systemd-private directories, which are normal boot artifacts, not executor residue). No unnecessary, unreverted, or security-weakening mutations were identified.
